title: Operations Toolkit & Policy Matrix — company-wide processes and templates
author: Samantha Ortiz
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page consolidates company-wide, cross-functional policies and ready-to-use templates for day-to-day operations: access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policy, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees and team leads to reduce decision friction and accelerate approvals.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and approved third parties. For customer-sensitive or legal-restricted guidance (e.g., export controls, regulated data), consult the corresponding restricted policy pages linked in Related pages.

Owner & Review cadence
- Primary owner: Finance & Legal (policy maintenance and procurement thresholds)
- Co-owners: Security (access control, data handling), People Ops (travel, expense policy), Eng SRE (change-management runbooks)
- Review cadence: Quarterly policy review; emergency revisions approved by two co-owners.

Table of Contents
1) Access & Permissions
2) Change Management
3) Data Management
4) Procurement & Expenses
5) Vendor Management and Onboarding
6) Travel & Expense Policy (quick summary + template)
7) Internal Templates and Examples
8) How to request exceptions

1) Access & Permissions
Intro: We use role-based access control (RBAC) for all production systems and principle of least privilege for internal systems. Key services: Okta (identity), AWS IAM (cloud resources), GCP IAM (where applicable), GitHub org, Confluence/JIRA.

Standards and SLAs
- New employee provisioning: People Ops initiates a provisioning request in Okta within 24 hours of start date. Typical completion SLA: 48 hours for standard roles.
- Access request SLA: 72 hours for non-urgent requests (standard escalation path); emergency escalations handled via oncall@redwood.com with 2-hour target.
- Review cadence: Role membership and privileged group audits every 90 days. Managers must confirm membership for direct reports.

Groups and ownership (examples)
- infra-admins (owner: eng-infra) — full terraform and cloud account access
- runtime-ops (owner: eng-serving-runtime) — runtime clusters and metrics dashboards (read/write where required)
- security-audit (owner: security-and-compliance) — read-only access to logs and audit trails

Request process (step-by-step)
1. Submit access request via the Access Request form (Confluence template link below) and attach manager approval.
2. Security performs privileged access justification review within 48 hours.
3. Provisioning completed by identity team (Okta) and changes logged to audit stream.

Temporary elevated access
- Temporary elevates granted only through short-lived sessions (Privileged Access Manager) and require time-bound justification and post-mortem within 7 days.

2) Change Management
Goal: Minimize customer impact by standardizing change windows, risk review, and rollback playbooks. System affected: anything labeled "production" in the service catalog.

Change Types
- Standard change: pre-approved, low-risk (e.g., routine certificate rotation). No RFC required, but must be logged.
- Normal change (RFC required): code rollouts, infra changes beyond 10% capacity shifts, major config changes.
- Emergency change: immediate action needed to prevent/mitigate customer impact.

Process (normal change)
1. Create RFC in JIRA using the "Change Request" issue type. Include risk assessment, rollback plan, and monitoring checklist.
2. Submit to change-review Slack channel and tag owners (service, SRE, security).
3. Change Advisory Board (CAB) evaluates changes >= P2 impact; CAB meets twice daily during major releases and weekly for routine batch reviews.
4. Approvals: owner, SRE lead, security reviewer. Approvals must be documented in the RFC.
5. Schedule change during approved window (default windows: Mon–Thu 02:00–05:00 PT for low-latency services; exceptions require exec sign-off).
6. Execute, monitor for 60 minutes at minimum (SLO: error rate <= baseline + 1.5x).
7. Post-change review within 5 business days if any anomaly detected; otherwise, note completion in RFC.

Emergency change rules
- Emergency RFC after-the-fact must be filed within 24 hours for audit.
- All emergency changes require a saturating post-mortem within 72 hours if outage threshold exceeded.

Rollback & Canary guidance
- All rollouts must support incremental canary with automatic rollback thresholds: if P99 latency increases >30% or error rate doubles, auto-rollback is triggered.

3) Data Management
Principles: classify, minimize, protect. Data classification levels: PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, RESTRICTED. Specific handling rules are in the Data Classification Reference (link).

Key controls
- Minimal retention: logs kept 90 days by default; analytics aggregates retained 3 years. Longer retention requires documented business justification and approval.
- Encryption: at-rest and in-transit required for CONFIDENTIAL and above. Key management via KMS (customer-managed optional for Private deployments).
- Backups: daily snapshots for critical services; restore exercise quarterly. RTO target: 4 hours for critical services; RPO: 1 hour.

Data access requests
- Use the Data Access Request template. Include dataset, purpose, time-bounded access, and manager sign-off. Security and Data Steward approvals required for CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED data.

Data deletion and exports
- Exports of customer data: require DPA review and explicit customer consent unless otherwise contractually allowed.
- Data deletion requests follow the Data Deletion Procedure and are tracked in the Data Compliance queue.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Objective: enable teams to move quickly while maintaining budget control and vendor risk mitigation. Procurement system: "ProcureHub" (internal). Expense submission: Expensr (employee-facing).

Approval matrix (quick reference)
| Amount (USD) | Required Approvals | Procurement Path |
|--------------|--------------------|-----------------|
| < 1,000 | Team manager | Team credit card or Expensr receipt upload |
| 1,000 - 10,000 | Manager + Finance reviewer | ProcureHub purchase order |
| 10,001 - 50,000 | Manager + Finance + Legal | ProcureHub + Vendor legal review |
| > 50,000 | Exec sponsor + Finance + Legal + Procurement lead | Procurement committee approval (2-week standard SLA) |

Standard procurement steps
1. Determine spend bucket and attach cost estimate to request.
2. Complete ProcureHub requisition with justification, owner, and accounting code.
3. Finance validates budget and issues PO when applicable.
4. Vendor contract review by Legal if > $10k or if data will be shared.
5. Invoice processing: invoices assigned an AP ticket; payment net-30 unless other terms negotiated.

Travel & Expenses summary (details below and templates included)
- Per diem: domestic USD 75/day for meals; international varies by country (see Travel per-diem table).
- Lodging: business-class hotel up to $250/night domestically; upgrades require manager approval.
- Air travel: economy for flights under 6 hours; premium economy/comfort for flights >6 hours with manager pre-approval.
- Receipts required for any item > $25. Alcohol is reimbursable only when accompanying business meals and within per-diem.

Expense submission SLA
- Employees must submit expenses within 30 days of travel/expense; Finance processes reimbursements within 15 business days of approved submission.

5) Vendor Management and Onboarding
Purpose: standardize vendor risk assessment, security questionnaires, and contract lifecycle.

Vendor risk categories
- Low: SaaS tools without access to customer data (e.g., marketing tools).
- Medium: vendors with access to internal data or identity systems (e.g., SSO integrations, analytics).
- High: vendors handling customer data, production systems, or infrastructure (e.g., hosting, third-party inference accelerators).

Onboarding checklist (must be completed before go-live for Medium/High vendors)
1. Vendor intake form in ProcureHub with product description, vendor contact, and contract value.
2. Security questionnaire (SIG-lite) completed and reviewed by Security.
3. Legal accepts contract terms or negotiates addenda (Data Processing Addendum if applicable).
4. Finance confirms billing terms and GL code.
5. Technical integration smoke test and runbook for incident response.
6. Assign vendor owner and schedule 90-day review after launch.

Contract renewal & offboarding
- Vendors are reviewed 60 days prior to renewal. Offboarding requires revoking keys, terminating accounts, and validating data deletion per contract terms.

6) Travel & Expense Policy — quick reference + template links
- Booking: Employees should use corporate travel provider where available. If using personal card, notify Finance and submit via Expensr within 30 days.
- International travel: ensure passport validity >= 6 months; complete travel safety form and get manager sign-off.
- Insurance: company travel insurance is enabled for all approved business trips.

Sample expense categories (for Expensr tagging): meals, lodging, transport, client-entertainment, equipment (< $2,000), training.

7) Internal Templates and Examples (links are CC placeholders)
- Access Request template: [Confluence Template] (link) — includes justification, role, and manager sign-off fields.
- Data Access Request template: [Confluence Template] (link) — includes dataset, purpose, retention, approval chain.
- Change RFC template (JIRA): pre-filled checklist for rollback, monitoring, and postmortem triggers.
- Procurement requisition: ProcureHub pre-approved fields and contractor classification checklist.
- Expense report template (Expensr): required fields: expense date, category, amount, merchant, purpose, attendee list (if client entertainment), receipt file.

Example: Access Request template fields
| Field | Required? | Notes |
|-------|-----------|-------|
| Requestor | Yes | Auto-filled from SSO |
| Role / Group | Yes | Select from canonical groups |
| Justification | Yes | Business reason and duration |
| Manager Approval | Yes | Manager email and signature (digital) |

8) How to request exceptions
- Non-standard exceptions (e.g., extended data retention, special vendor terms) must be submitted via the Exception Request form and include: business justification, risk mitigation plan, and duration.
- Approval path: owner_team -> Finance -> Legal -> Head of relevant org. For security-sensitive exceptions an additional Security & Compliance review applies.

Governance & Audit
- All changes, procurement, and access modifications are logged. Quarterly audit reports produced by Finance and Security, presented at the Operational Review.
- Policy violations escalated to People Ops and may result in remedial training or access removal.

Appendix: Quick links and commands
- Create RFC (JIRA): Create -> Issue -> Type: Change Request
- Access request template (Confluence): Templates -> Access Requests -> "New"
- ProcureHub requisition: https://procurehub.redwood.internal/ (internal)
- Expense submission: Expensr mobile / web portal (link in People Ops handbook)

Contact & escalation
- Policy questions: policy-questions@redwood.com
- Procurement & vendor intake: procurement@redwood.com
- Security exceptions: security-exceptions@redwood.com
- Immediate operational emergencies: oncall@redwood.com (use for incidents only)

Change log

Notes & next steps
- Teams should adopt the templates by Q2 2026 and migrate legacy procurement flows to ProcureHub. Security will publish an automated audit report in the Security Dashboard by end of Q1 2026.
